items.question: What service levels does Schedule 2 of the MSA set?
items.answer:
Schedule 2 of the MSA sets the service levels for the Services provided by the Provider. According to the MSA, the Provider must make the Services available at least 99.5% of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance notified at least five business days in advance [2].

The specific service levels related to availability are outlined in the side letter, which is referenced in the MSA. The side letter specifies that for each full hour of unavailability below the 99.5% level, the Client will receive a service credit of 5% of the monthly subscription fee [2].

Additionally, service credits in any calendar month are capped at 25% of the monthly subscription fee for that month [2].

evidence.quote: Provider will make the Services available at least 99.5% of each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance notified at least five (5) business days in advance.
For each full hour of unavailability below that level, Client will receive a service credit of five percent (5%) of the monthly subscription fee.
Service credits in any calendar month are capped at twenty-five percent (25%) of the monthly subscription fee for that month.

items.question: Is the Beta Corp settlement confidential?
items.answer:
